caption: The drawing depicts a single object, which appears to be a small pot or saucepan with a long handle. The body of the pot is bulbous with a slight narrowing near the top, and it has a short spout protruding from the side, featuring a rounded tip beneath the spout. The handle is long and slender, extending upwards and to the right from the pot, with a bulbous end that tapers before connecting to the pot. The handle also has a slight widening and a ring-like detail near the end attached to the pot. The drawing is executed in pencil on off-white or slightly yellowed paper, with shading to suggest the metallic or reflective quality of the pot and the wooden or textured character of the handle. In the lower right corner, there is a small inset line drawing of the same object, showing its basic outline and proportions. The artist's name "Amelia Tuccio" and the year "1936" are inscribed in the lower left corner. The entire composition is centered on the page, with the primary pot and handle rendered in detailed shading and the inset in simple line work.
title: Silver Pipkin
